messages.author: 72f2ccabe1e5089f
messages.subject: Multi-session mixture models
parts:
Hi
I am trying to fit a multi-session model using the hcov argument to include sex in the models. I have got 12 sessions and each session-specific trap object has a usage matrix. I am getting the following error message:

mixture models fail when the first detector is not 
                        used on the first day

The message is clear but it is not possible for me to resolve the issue by reordering the traps. The sessions are temporal and there are no detectors that were operating on the first day of each and every session. 

I'm not sure if the only solution is to either:
1) insert a 1 into the first entry of all the usage matrices. Obviously this is wrong but I would imagine is likely to have little impact on the resulting estimates.
2) use a different approach (like using the group argument) for the modelling of sex.

I have observed sex values for all captures so am thinking that I should use the groups = "sex" approach to get around the problem as my understanding is that the two approaches are equivalent. But regardless of that, as a matter of interest is it possible to get hcov to work when it is not possible to have the first trap operating on the first day in all sessions?

Many thanks.

Greg

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session mixture models
parts:
I will dig sometime (next month?) and find out why I stuck in that odd restriction and message - it was probably a lazy way around some trivial issue that can be fixed. Meantime, it would indeed be extraordinary if fudging that one 'usage' value made more than a trivial difference. I would go to sex as a covariate (CL = TRUE) before using groups, but I guess you are wanting to model density...
Murray

messages.author: 72f2ccabe1e5089f
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session mixture models
parts:
Hi Murray and thanks as always for the rapid response.
The main objective is to model density and so as I understand things I need to use the FL to try out different types of density models across sessions, but as a matter of interest why do you suggest using the CL and rather including sex as an individual covariate? I know there are various ways to model something like sex but am not that clear on the relative advantages and disadvantages. One thing I noticed while playing around (and fudging the usage matrix) was that I got quite different density estimates from using the hcov vs the groups approach to include sex. I was expecting similar results. Would you say the most likely reason is a local maximum with the h2 model? And if so that using groups may be a more stable approach?

Last thing, I'm just playing around fitting some single session models but have noticed that most of them show an AIC value but an NA for AICc. I would have thought that if there is valid info to calculate AIC then there is no reason why one could not calculate AICc?

Thanks a lot

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Multi-session mixture models
parts:
Hi Greg
I attach an old pdf that may gives some clues to my prejudice against groups (less stable code, as sometimes revealed on this list).

Remember the hcov approach estimates combined density of both sexes together, and the default with groups = 'sex' (D~1) is to assume 50:50 group (sex) mixture.

The AIC code includes this line:
    AICcval <- ifelse ((n - Npar - 1)>0,
                       2*(secr$fit$value + Npar) + 2 * Npar * (Npar+1) / (n - Npar - 1),
                       NA)

Maybe you have a lot of parameters (Npar) and not many animals (n)?
Murray
